title: QUIC Advisory msquic Peer-Blocked Evidence Classification Architecture
purpose: Describe the advisory classification lane that keeps the preserved msquic major-peer failures tagged as peer-side blocked evidence while the quic-go client download-liveness slice remains the only local candidate.
design_summary: The major-peer evidence already splits msquic failures into peer-tls-alert-50 and peer-connection-terminated classes. This architecture formalizes that cluster as blocked evidence rather than a local transport bug, keeps it separate from the quic-go download-liveness candidate, and preserves the advisory boundary so the matrix remains a reporting surface rather than support proof.
alternatives_considered: Treat the msquic TLS alert cluster as a local Incursa transport defect. Rejected because the preserved evidence still points at peer-side handshake and termination noise.
Fold the msquic rows into the quic-go download-liveness candidate. Rejected because the failure classes are different and should remain distinguishable.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Preserve the peer-side outcome classes from the current evidence run.
Do not recast the cluster as support evidence without new host or peer data.
Keep the lane advisory and outside ordinary gating.
Keep the lane separate from the local quic-go candidate.
data_and_state_considerations: The slice relies on the preserved major-peer evidence report and current repo-local trace notes. It does not require runtime changes to stay formalized.
risks: Readers may overread the blocked classification as a fix if the advisory boundary is not kept explicit.
The line between peer-side blocked evidence and local candidate work can blur if the lane is reused for runtime debugging.

supplemental_sections.heading: Scope
supplemental_sections.content: This design only formalizes the blocked classification lane. It does not assert msquic support or change the major-peer matrix profile.
